segments.he: הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶן מְשַׂחֵק בְּקוּבְיָא. הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? תְּנָא פְּסוּלָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְקָתָנֵי פְּסוּלָא דְּרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If «one of» the litigants «was a dice player,» or one who lends with interest, or among those who fly pigeons, or among the vendors of produce that grew during the Sabbatical Year, then the litigant opposing him takes an oath and receives payment of his claim. The Gemara asks: «Why do I» need «these additional» examples of a person who is suspect with regard to oath taking? The Gemara explains: The mishna first «teaches» examples of people who are «disqualified by Torah law, and» then «teaches» examples of those who are «disqualified by rabbinic law.»
